name: Cross-Entropy Benchmarking (XEB)
algorithm: Linear cross-entropy on random quantum circuits
description: Cross-entropy benchmarking (XEB) is a statistical method for evaluating quantum processor performance by measuring how well experimental output distributions of random circuits correlate with ideal distributions. Google used linear XEB to demonstrate quantum computational advantage on the 53-qubit Sycamore processor in 2019. The XEB fidelity decays exponentially with circuit depth, providing a measure of cumulative gate quality.
significance: The benchmark behind Google's 2019 quantum supremacy claim, establishing cross-entropy as the primary metric for quantum computational advantage demonstrations.

news.title: IBM and UChicago Advance Trusted Quantum Computing with Verified Logical Circuits
news.excerpt: IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago announced a demonstration in quantum computing that achieves the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage: performing computations beyond the reach of leading classical simulation methods while providing trust that the computation returned accurate results.

news.title: IBM and UChicago Demonstrate Quantum Advantage via XEB-Verified Fidelity on 70 Logical Qubits
news.excerpt: IBM and University of Chicago researchers used XEB-based fidelity verification to demonstrate quantum advantage using 70 logical qubits in a depth-70 Clifford+T circuit with 468 T gates and 2,415 two-qubit logical operations, achieving logical error rates 10× lower than underlying physical error rates.
